role: dated access review; not deployment authority
scoreScope: Current live production readiness: development-open policies would permit unauthorized access if treated as production security. This is not a code-quality score.
summary: Product public reads and protected media blockers are closed in source and local tests. Domain commands reuse existing authority and Core upload mechanics. The production gate now requires both reviewed live policy sources, but no deployment, live policy update or live data write was performed. Live development-open permissions remain a release blocker.

findings.issue: The live named Firestore database and Storage bucket Rules both allow read and write if true. The Firestore policy is the explicitly accepted development policy; neither is production privacy.
findings.recommendation: Keep deployment withheld. Prepare and approve separate Firestore and Storage rollouts with exact target backups and readback; do not silently alter the development policy.

findings.issue: The prior candidate allowed raw public Product roots containing provisioning state.
findings.recommendation: Closed locally: public collection/detail APIs use a shared allowlisted server projection, including safe public prices. Raw roots/prices are admin-only in the candidate. Admin Firebase readers and provider retry ownership are preserved.

findings.issue: The prior candidate permitted direct Blog, Product and provider-price writes despite their trusted command owners. This could bypass editorial review, reservation and provider reconciliation.
findings.recommendation: Closed locally: direct create/update/delete is now denied, with current command tests and allow/deny regressions. Live permissions remain unchanged.

findings.issue: The prior browser upload paths could not use membership-bound authority from the named misebox database in Storage Rules.
findings.recommendation: Closed locally: Place, Ingredient, Blog, Product and Professional image callers select protected domain commands. Core decodes/re-encodes image bytes, saves unique revisions and rechecks authority before returning a URL. The separate native-tested Storage candidate denies SDK reads/writes while explicit public image tokens work. No membership mirror or live permission change was introduced.

localProductDiagnostic.scope: local demo emulator only; repaired source-policy regression
localProductDiagnostic.publicServerProjection: allowlisted; provisioning, audit identities and provider metadata excluded

liveGrantPrerequisites.scope: canonical Kitchen grant entries for the six supported Apps; read only

checks.ingress: ALLOW_ALL; public website ingress, not command authorization
checks.nativeProductionPreflight: passed locally with both demo emulators

storagePolicy.browserSDK: read/list/create/overwrite/delete denied for anonymous and authenticated requests

limits: No deployment, live write, Rules change or IAM change was performed.
Runtime service-account direct project bindings were inspected; inherited IAM, bucket-level IAM and signed URL/download-token lifecycle were not exhaustively certified.
Tests prove their encoded cases, not all Apps, routes or commercial/provider journeys.
The live grant inventory found one canonical index and one matching supported-App entry; it does not infer or create additional operator grants.
nextAttack: Review historical download-token exposure and inherited/bucket IAM before approving production policy rollout.
Separately authorize backed-up, exact-target Firestore and Storage policy rollout and readback.
Only then approve an application release; no deployment is authorized by this audit.
